subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog and recovery surface, and which recovery actions should be default, opt-in, or out of scope?
rationale: The remaining work crosses process supervision, config/defaults, doctor repair authority, notifications, degraded startup, health protocol, and security-sensitive operator actions, so a source-level review cannot choose the permanent product semantics safely.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Opt-In Recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

options.title: Supersede With Narrow Canonicals
options.body: Close this broad item only after explicit canonical issues cover process watchdog, health schema, error policy, degraded startup, and notifications.

options.title: Decline Core Recovery Ownership
options.body: Document supervisor, plugin, or ClawHub patterns instead of adding core-owned recovery behavior for now.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Opt-In Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current main-only crash-loop breaker and has the broadest recent history across the overlapping Gateway startup, health, channel suppression, and unhandled-error paths.
